note: Human decisions over the 99 items in needs-human.json that the agent reviewer could not settle. Grade scale matches the sheet: 3 answers the query, 2 substantially relevant, 1 touches the subject, 0 not relevant. Following session 7's applied HIGH calls, 1 is used for on-topic-but-does-not-answer and 0 is reserved for items that are not about the subject at all. `why` is the reason the grade rests on and is the durable half of this pass — review.md can only carry the number. The ledger also carries adjustments to calls applied in an earlier pass; those entries are marked outside_pool and are not part of the 99.
rules: Grade against the query as a literal search, benchmarked against the items already graded 3 for that query. The question is 'would this at rank 1 have answered it', not 'is this a good tool'.
A grade belongs to a (query, item) pair. An item that answers a different query is not promoted here on that account — it already scores where it belongs.

Near-duplicates are handled by an equivalence class, not by a grade. Items that are one answer at two URLs share a `group` label and every metric counts the group once: either copy is a full answer, returning both earns nothing extra, and the ideal ranking holds one representative. Each member keeps the grade its own document earns. This replaces the canonical-and-echo stopgap, which demoted the echo to 1 — that approximated the same arithmetic but understated nDCG when a method returned the echo, and encoded identity as a grade, which the next re-judging pass would have silently undone. A repo and a third party's article about it are NOT one product and are graded independently.
Grade from the mechanism the document ships, not from framing that reuses the query's vocabulary. This was the agent reviewer's leading error.
A real capability bundled inside a larger product is 1, not 0. A claim with no mechanism is 1. Only an item off the subject entirely is 0.
